paid:2021-3.memo: The 48-to-60 paid factor of 1.098 sits 6 points above the clean norm of 1.037. Half of the excess is one large loss still paying instalments (two notes, 5.2 points); that is one-off and belongs in the large-loss load. A further 2.5 points is inflation on sixteen litigated and medical files, with the same fee-schedule and verdict language seen on every open accident year this calendar year, and it is partly masked by a 2-point subrogation credit and a small fast-track timing effect. Ten files also carry 2025 reserve-review notes, which affect reported rather than paid. Carry about 1.062: norm plus the inflation, with the large loss, the recovery and the timing stripped.

paid:2022-2.memo: The 36-to-48 paid factor of 1.184 against a clean norm of 1.099 is mostly timing. Fifteen files settled under the 2025 fast-track programme at their case reserve, about a year earlier than the pattern, worth 5.2 points. Inflation language on 22 files adds 1.2 points and is recurring. The reported factor moves far less and closed counts jump, which confirms the timing reading. A 2-point residual is not explained by the notes. Carry about 1.111: strip the timing, keep the inflation, and revise the payment pattern if the programme continues rather than carrying a higher factor.

The large losses go to the large-loss load, the timing to a revised pattern. At this immaturity the Bornhuetter-Ferguson method should carry more weight than either development method.

incurred:2023-1.memo: The 24-to-36 reported factor of 1.154 is 10 points above the clean norm of 1.053. Two large losses explain 10.4 points, inflation on thirty files 5.4 points, and the reserve review 1.6 points. The negative residual shows the untagged files developed below norm, consistent with the fast-track programme releasing case reserves on small claims as they closed. Carry about 1.108: norm plus inflation, with the large losses and the strengthening stripped.

col:paid:0.memo: Almost every accident year in the 12-to-24 column carries a large loss paying out early, worth between 10 and 43 points, so the unadjusted average of 2.101 is dominated by them. Stripping the large losses, the 2020 court-closure slow-down (and its 2019 counterpart on the other side), the 2024 fast-track timing and the small recoveries brings the adjusted average to 1.818. Inflation on AY 2022 to 2024 stays in and is rising year on year. Select about 1.818 and handle large losses through a separate load; this column is too volatile to carry raw. Watch whether the 2024 fast-track timing persists into the next diagonal.

col:paid:1.memo: The 24-to-36 column moves from 1.320 unadjusted to 1.226 once one-off movements are removed. Large losses appear in five of the eight years; the 2020 slow-down shows as a deferral in AY 2018 and a catch-up in AY 2019; AY 2023 adds a fast-track timing effect. Inflation is present and growing in AY 2021 to 2023 and is kept. Select 1.226. The adjusted factors are tighter than the raw ones, which is the point of the exercise: the remaining spread is genuine development, not events.

col:paid:2.memo: The 36-to-48 column drops from 1.140 to 1.107 after stripping large losses in three years, a recovery in AY 2020, the slow-down pair in AY 2017 and 2018, and the AY 2022 fast-track timing. Inflation in AY 2021 and 2022 stays in. Select 1.107. The pattern of inflation only in the two most recent years at this age is the calendar-year signal: it is 2024 and 2025 experience, not accident-year experience, and will reach the older years as they develop.

col:paid:3.memo: The 48-to-60 column is quiet apart from AY 2021, whose 1.097 includes a large loss, a recovery and a small timing effect alongside 2.5 points of inflation. Adjusted, AY 2021 is 1.059 and the column average 1.043 against 1.053 unadjusted. Select 1.043. Note that even at this age the 2025 inflation is visible on litigated files; the tail factor should carry it too.

col:incurred:0.memo: The 12-to-24 reported column moves from 1.441 to 1.303 after stripping large losses in seven years, the slow-down pair in AY 2019 and 2020, and the 2025 reserve strengthening in AY 2024. Inflation in AY 2022 to 2024 is kept. Select 1.303, but with a caveat: AY 2024 reserves now sit on the strengthened basis and will develop less than this history, so either restate prior years' case reserves to the current adequacy level or lean on the paid and Bornhuetter-Ferguson methods for the two youngest years.

col:incurred:1.memo: The 24-to-36 reported column drops from 1.116 to 1.055 once large losses in five years, the slow-down pair and the AY 2023 strengthening are removed. Inflation in AY 2021 to 2023 is kept and is growing. Select 1.055. The adjusted AY 2019 factor below 1.0 reflects case releases after its large loss settled; that is genuine and should stay.
